article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Heirloom Swiss Strawberry × Sorbet
Breeder: DNA Genetics
THC Content: 23%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Strawberry candy, sweet fruit, cream
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: 500–650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500–650 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Strawberry Sorbet smells less like a bowl of fresh berries than a concentrated version of everything people associate with strawberry-flavored candy. The sweetness can be immediate and almost confectionary, yet underneath it sits enough earth, pine, wood, and subtle fuel to remind the consumer that this is resin-heavy marijuana rather than a one-dimensional fruit novelty. DNA Genetics created the cultivar by combining Heirloom Swiss Strawberry with its Sorbet line, building an indica-dominant plant around intense flavor, fast flowering, abundant resin, and enough production to make the genetics useful beyond small connoisseur gardens.

That resin is an important part of the strain’s identity. DNA Genetics specifically highlights Strawberry Sorbet for hash and concentrate production, and mature plants can become extremely sticky as the dark green flowers fill with trichomes. The cultivar finishes in about nine weeks, produces above-average yields, and develops a calm, happy effect with enough mental brightness to encourage creativity and awareness rather than immediately pushing the consumer toward sleep. For growers who want strawberry-forward weed without sacrificing structure, harvest weight, or extraction potential, the strain offers an unusually complete package.
Genetics and Lineage

The official pedigree is Heirloom Swiss Strawberry × Sorbet. DNA Genetics does not publish a detailed deeper family tree for the Heirloom Swiss Strawberry parent, so its identity is best preserved as the breeder presents it rather than attaching speculative ancestry. Its contribution is easy to recognize in the finished cross, however. The parent supplies the pronounced strawberry direction, fruit sweetness, and much of the aromatic personality that separates this cannabis strain from DNA’s other Sorbet hybrids.

Sorbet represents the modern dessert side of the pairing. DNA Genetics has used the line repeatedly in cultivars such as Banana Sorbet , Sour Sorbet, Gelato Sorbet-related projects, and several other crosses selected around resin, flower quality, and soft sweet flavors. Within Strawberry Sorbet, it adds density, trichome production, a smoother dessert character, and enough structural influence to keep the plant manageable. Rather than overwhelming the Heirloom Swiss Strawberry, the Sorbet side gives the fruit profile a creamier and more polished background.

DNA Genetics classifies the finished strain at approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. That relatively close split explains why the plant remains vigorous without becoming excessively tall and why the effect combines mental brightness with physical ease. The genetics are dessert oriented, but the earthy pine and mild fuel notes prevent the final flower from feeling disconnected from more traditional cannabis. This balance between old fruit character and contemporary resin-focused breeding is central to Strawberry Sorbet’s appeal.
Effects and Experience

The initial experience tends to feel cheerful rather than overwhelming. Mood can rise quickly, ordinary surroundings seem more interesting, and conversation or creative activity may become easier to settle into. DNA Genetics describes the effect as happy and peaceful while also emphasizing increased creativity and awareness, an unusual combination for a cultivar carrying a clear indica majority. Moderate consumption generally allows that brighter mental phase to remain noticeable before stronger physical relaxation develops.

As the session continues, the body becomes calmer without necessarily becoming immediately heavy. Muscles loosen, the pace of activity slows, and the earlier mental enthusiasm settles into a more comfortable state. This progression makes the cultivar adaptable to low-pressure social settings, music, drawing, gaming, movies, or an evening spent unwinding without wanting an instant couch-lock experience. Higher doses naturally bring the physical side forward more strongly and can make the later stages noticeably sleepier.

Because DNA Genetics does not publish one universal THC number for the seed line, potency should be judged from the actual harvest whenever laboratory testing is available. Resin-heavy flower can still produce a substantial experience even without a headline cannabinoid figure. Consumers with lower tolerance should start conservatively, particularly because the sweet strawberry flavor can make repeated consumption deceptively easy. Excessive intake may cause dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, mental haze, or temporary anxiety before the more peaceful effects become dominant.
Medical Benefits

The blend of positive mental effects and gradual physical relaxation may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who dislike strains that immediately become sedating. During the earlier portion of the experience, the happier and more engaged headspace may make stress, emotional fatigue, or low motivation feel less intrusive. Because mental awareness remains comparatively intact at moderate servings, some consumers may find the cultivar easier to use during the transition from daytime responsibilities into a relaxed evening.

Physical calm becomes more relevant later. General tension and muscular discomfort may fade into the background, while larger doses can increase appetite and encourage rest. That changing character makes dosage particularly important. A smaller serving may feel socially comfortable and creatively stimulating, whereas a stronger amount can move much closer to traditional indica relaxation.

Neither the cannabinoid profile nor the terpene chemistry is standardized across every Strawberry Sorbet plant. Medical marijuana consumers should therefore avoid assuming that all batches will produce identical results simply because they share the same cultivar name. Laboratory information from the specific flower, personal THC tolerance, medications, and previous reactions to cannabis provide a more reliable basis for therapeutic use than generalized strain descriptions.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Strawberry dominates the bouquet, but the character often leans toward ripe fruit and candy rather than the delicate aroma of a freshly cut berry. DNA Genetics describes an intense sweet-candy profile reminiscent of a strawberry field, and well-grown flowers can produce enough fragrance to become conspicuous before the buds are even broken apart. The sweetness is dense rather than sharp, giving the aroma a rounded quality that fits naturally with the Sorbet side of the pedigree.

Earth, pine, and wood emerge beneath that fruit and keep the bouquet grounded. These secondary notes become easier to detect as mature flowers are handled or ground, when sticky resin releases a deeper cannabis aroma beneath the strawberry sweetness. Light fuel can appear on the finish, providing just enough pungency to prevent the strain from becoming entirely dessert-like. Phenotypes may differ in how strongly they emphasize the strawberry versus the earthier background.

Flavor follows the same general architecture. Sweet strawberry and fruit appear first, while pine and earth become more noticeable through the middle of the inhale. A subtle fuel or woody character can remain after exhalation. Vaporization tends to preserve more of the bright fruit and sweet compounds, whereas combustion emphasizes resin, earth, and pine. A slow dry and careful cure are especially important because the strawberry top notes can be diminished quickly by excessive heat or rushed post-harvest handling.
Growing Information

Strawberry Sorbet is a vigorous but manageable photoperiod plant. DNA Genetics lists indoor height around three to five feet and outdoor height around four to six feet, giving growers enough vertical growth for strong production without the extreme stretch associated with tall sativa varieties. The plant responds well to topping and low-stress training, both of which help distribute light across the canopy and encourage multiple productive branches rather than allowing one dominant top to control the garden.

Flowering takes approximately nine weeks, with breeder-listed indoor yields around 500–650 g/m². Strawberry Sorbet is specifically described as a very heavy feeder, so healthy plants require consistent access to macro- and micronutrients as flower production accelerates. Growers should still avoid confusing heavy nutrient demand with indiscriminate overfeeding; irrigation, root-zone conditions, and plant response remain better guides than a fixed nutrient strength. Branch support can become useful late in bloom as the resinous buds gain weight.

Outdoor plants can produce roughly 500–650 grams each and typically finish around late October in favorable Northern Hemisphere climates. DNA Genetics describes the cultivar as sturdy, resilient, and relatively resistant to common diseases and pests, qualities that make it approachable for less experienced growers. Warm climates with long sunny summers are ideal, although greenhouse cultivation can provide additional environmental control. The large resin output also makes the harvest particularly attractive for dry sift, ice-water hash, rosin, and other concentrate methods.
FAQ
What strains make Strawberry Sorbet?

Strawberry Sorbet was bred by DNA Genetics from Heirloom Swiss Strawberry × Sorbet. The strawberry parent supplies the pronounced fruit identity, while Sorbet contributes dessert sweetness, resin production, and modern flower quality.
Is Strawberry Sorbet indica or sativa?

DNA Genetics classifies the cultivar at approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. Its structure remains manageable and productive, while the effects combine peaceful physical relaxation with a noticeable amount of mental brightness and creativity.
What does Strawberry Sorbet taste like?

The primary flavor is sweet strawberry candy accompanied by ripe fruit, earth, pine, wood, and subtle fuel. The strawberry note dominates, but the deeper herbal and resinous qualities keep the finished flower from tasting purely sugary.
How long does Strawberry Sorbet take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately nine weeks. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity around late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Is Strawberry Sorbet good for making hash and concentrates?

Yes. DNA Genetics specifically recommends the cultivar for concentrate and hash makers because of its very heavy resin production. Mature flowers become exceptionally sticky and trichome rich, making well-selected plants attractive for dry sift, ice-water hash, and solventless rosin.
Final Thoughts on Strawberry Sorbet

Strawberry Sorbet succeeds by giving fruit-forward cannabis more substance than flavor alone. Heirloom Swiss Strawberry provides the unmistakable ripe strawberry and candy identity, while Sorbet adds resin, flower density, dessert softness, and a more contemporary finish. Earth, pine, wood, and mild fuel remain underneath the sweetness, allowing the profile to stay recognizably cannabis even at its fruitiest.

The cultivation characteristics are equally important. A nine-week flowering period, approximately 500–650 g/m² indoors, similar potential per outdoor plant, manageable height, and strong natural resilience create a cultivar with genuine production value. Its heavy appetite requires attentive feeding, but straightforward training and sturdy growth keep the plant accessible to cultivators who have not yet mastered more difficult genetics.

For consumers, the experience mirrors the strain’s balanced genetic ratio. Happiness, creativity, and awareness appear early, followed by a peaceful physical calm that becomes deeper as the dose rises. Combined with exceptional resin production and a strawberry-candy profile that remains distinctive after curing, Strawberry Sorbet stands as one of DNA Genetics’ more complete Sorbet-family hybrids—a strain capable of satisfying fruit enthusiasts, flower growers, and hash makers without relying on one characteristic alone.
